prompt.context_jp: 隣に立つ東海林の視線___、痛いほど背中に注がれる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隣に立つ東海林の視線___、痛いほど背中に注がれる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits: a new sensory detail introduced into the scene.

feedback.correct_en: The gaze is newly introduced as a subject being felt — neutral description of a new element in the scene calls for が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the gaze as an already-established topic being contrasted. を is wrong because 注がれる is passive; the gaze is the one doing the pouring.

contrast_examples.en: As for the gaze, it was cold. (topic already known)

prompt.context_jp: ハケン弁当の企画___、東海林一人のものではない。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハケン弁当の企画___、東海林一人のものではない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: the sentence states what the project is/isn't as its theme.

feedback.correct_en: The Haken bento project is the established topic Satonaka is thinking about; は marks it as the theme being characterized.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as brand-new information, but here it's already the focus of his thoughts. を doesn't fit this nominal predicate structure.

contrast_examples.jp: この企画は私のものだ。

prompt.context_jp: 周囲の空気___凍りつく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 周囲の空気___凍りつく。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: a sudden, newly observed event.

feedback.correct_en: This is a neutral description of a sudden change — the air freezing is new information unfolding in the scene, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would suggest a contrastive topic ('as for the air...'), awkward for a sudden event. に marks destination/time, not the subject.

prompt.context_jp: 手書きの文字___、几帳面な角ばりで並んでいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 手書きの文字___、几帳面な角ばりで並んでいる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: describing what Ogasawara is noticing on the paper.

feedback.correct_en: Ogasawara is noticing the handwritten characters as a new discovery — neutral description with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the characters an established topic being contrasted with something else, which doesn't match this fresh observation.

contrast_examples.en: The characters (as topic) are hard to read.

prompt.context_jp: 「ケータイの電話番号___書いてあるぞ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ケータイの電話番号___書いてあるぞ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: announcing a new discovery on the paper.

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is announcing newly-spotted information. が marks the subject of this fresh discovery.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the phone number was already under discussion as a topic. に would mark a location, not the thing being written.

contrast_examples.en: A number is written (I just noticed).
As for the number, it isn't written.

prompt.context_jp: 仕事の手___完全に止まっている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 仕事の手___完全に止まっている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: framing the general situation of work on the floor.

feedback.correct_en: This frames 'work' as a topic being characterized — everyone's hands have stopped. は presents it as the state of affairs, with an implicit contrast to the gossip.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as new information, but the narrative is characterizing an overall state, not reporting a sudden event.

contrast_examples.en: Work is at a standstill. (state as topic)

prompt.context_jp: 番号を押したの___、拾い主の小笠原自身である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 番号を押したの___、拾い主の小笠原自身である。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: identifying exactly who pressed the number.

feedback.correct_en: 'The one who pressed the number' is the topic being identified; は presents the known action and attributes it to Ogasawara.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be used in an exhaustive-listing cleft like '小笠原が押した' (it was Ogasawara who pressed). Here the structure 'Xのは Y だ' requires は.

contrast_examples.en: The one who pressed it is Ogasawara.
It was Ogasawara who pressed it.

prompt.context_jp: ところが、聞こえてきたの___意外な着信音だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ところが、聞こえてきたの___意外な着信音だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'What was heard was...' structure.

feedback.correct_en: 'What came to be heard' is set up as the topic, with the surprising revelation following. は fits this X-のは-Y pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly try to introduce 'the thing that was heard' as brand-new, but the structure here is an equational topic-comment.

contrast_examples.jp: 聞こえてきたのは音楽だった。

prompt.context_jp: 背後に___東海林の姿はない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 背後に___東海林の姿はない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: emphasizing that Shoji is specifically NOT behind him.

feedback.correct_en: に+は marks a contrastive location: 'behind him (as opposed to elsewhere), Shoji is not there.' This fits the lonely moment Satonaka feels.
feedback.incorrect_en: Plain に lacks the contrastive nuance the scene needs. が doesn't fit with location marking here.

contrast_examples.en: Here (of all places) there's no one.

prompt.context_jp: 「東海林主任___マーケティング課に 譲ってくれたんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「東海林主任___マーケティング課に 譲ってくれたんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: Satonaka is revealing WHO gave up the project.

feedback.correct_en: Satonaka is revealing a surprising fact — it was Chief Shoji who gave it to them. が marks the exhaustive/identifying subject in this revelation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make Shoji a pre-established topic, losing the surprise reveal. The 'news value' of the subject calls for が.

contrast_examples.en: It was Shoji who gave it up.

prompt.context_jp: 時計の針が午後を回っても、東海林の席___空いたままだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時計の針が午後を回っても、東海林の席___空いたままだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: characterizing the ongoing state of Shoji's seat.

feedback.correct_en: Shoji's seat is the known topic, and the sentence characterizes its state (still empty). は fits the contrastive-ish framing against the busy floor.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as new information, but his seat is already in everyone's awareness as the absent one.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の辞書___ "不可能"と "ヒューマンスキル"の文字はない
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の辞書___ "不可能"と "ヒューマンスキル"の文字はない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: the narrator sets up 'her dictionary' as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: に marks the location (in her dictionary) where these words don't exist. The topic-setting phrase 'in her dictionary' uses に.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the dictionary as subject, but the real subject is the words. を doesn't fit this existential structure.

contrast_examples.en: In the dictionary, there is no answer.

prompt.context_jp: 夕方になっても、東海林の携帯から___呼び出し音が返ってくるだけだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夕方になっても、東海林の携帯から___呼び出し音が返ってくるだけだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'from his phone (only)...'

feedback.correct_en: から+は creates a contrastive topic: from his phone (as opposed to from him personally), only the ring tone returned. Emphasizes the futility.
feedback.incorrect_en: Plain から without は loses the contrastive emphasis. が doesn't combine with から here.

prompt.context_jp: 春子は湯呑み___置き、しばらく無言のまま窓の外を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子は湯呑み___置き、しばらく無言のまま窓の外を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the direct object of 置く.

feedback.correct_en: 置く is a transitive verb; the teacup is the direct object being placed down, marked with を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the teacup the subject (as if it placed itself). に would mark a destination, not the object.

prompt.context_jp: その声を耳にした瞬間、里中の全身___固まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その声を耳にした瞬間、里中の全身___固まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: a sudden bodily event in response to the voice.

feedback.correct_en: The freezing of his body is a sudden, new reaction described neutrally — が marks the subject of this event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'his whole body' a topic being contrasted, losing the immediacy of the moment.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林の姿___、当然のことながら現れない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東海林の姿___、当然のことながら現れない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: Shoji is already the known subject of their wait.

feedback.correct_en: Shoji's figure is the expected topic they're waiting for; は marks him as the known subject whose absence is being commented on.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce him as new; but he's precisely who they're waiting for, making him the topic.

prompt.context_jp: そこに立っていたの___、しばらく姿を消していたはずの、あの人だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこに立っていたの___、しばらく姿を消していたはずの、あの人だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'the one standing there was...' cleft structure.

feedback.correct_en: The X-のは-Y だ cleft structure requires は: 'the one who was standing there' (topic) 'was that person' (comment).
feedback.incorrect_en: が in a cleft like this would be ungrammatical. This structure is reserved for は.

prompt.context_jp: 塵も___も山となるとは言うが、一枚の紙切れが、こうして瞬く間に噂の中心地を作り上げてしまう。
prompt.prompt_jp: 塵も___も山となる
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb (dust piled up becomes a mountain).

feedback.correct_en: The proverb is 塵も積もれば山となる — 'even dust, when it piles up, becomes a mountain.' 積もる is the fixed verb.
feedback.incorrect_en: 集める (to gather) and 重ねる (to stack) are semantically related but not part of the fixed proverb.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.

prompt.context_jp: 「プレゼンひっくり返して 私に恥かかして… ___に 手 噛まれたよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___に 手 噛まれたよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the idiom Kirishima uses about his betrayed trust in Shoji.

feedback.correct_en: 飼い犬に手を噛まれる is a set idiom meaning 'bitten by one's own pet dog' — betrayed by someone you raised/trusted. Fits Kirishima's feelings about Shoji.
feedback.incorrect_en: 野良犬 (stray) and 子犬 (puppy) break the fixed idiom; the whole point is that it's YOUR OWN dog.

contrast_examples.jp: 飼い犬に手を噛まれた。
contrast_examples.en: Bitten by my own dog (betrayed by a protégé).
Barked at by a stray. (literal, no idiom)

prompt.context_jp: 呼び出し音が鳴り始めた瞬間、誰もが息を___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰もが息を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the collocation: everyone held their breath.

feedback.correct_en: 息を潜める means 'to hold one's breath / hush' with the nuance of quiet anticipation, perfect for this tense moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を止める is more literal ('stop breathing'). 息を隠す is not a standard collocation.

prompt.context_jp: 里中は___を一つして、ネクタイの結び目をわずかに直した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 里中は___を一つして、ネクタイの結び目をわずかに直した。
prompt.prompt_en: Satonaka took a ___ to steady himself before presenting.

feedback.correct_en: 深呼吸 (deep breath) matches the preparation-before-presentation context. He's steadying his nerves.
feedback.incorrect_en: ため息 (sigh) would convey resignation, not focus. あくび (yawn) implies boredom.

contrast_examples.en: Take a deep breath to calm down.

prompt.context_jp: 「ちょっと 他の所に ___されちゃって そっちに行くことにしたんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ちょっと 他の所に ___されちゃって」
prompt.prompt_en: Shoji claims he was ___ by another company.

feedback.correct_en: ヘッドハンティング means being recruited/poached — Shoji is saving face by claiming he was headhunted.
feedback.incorrect_en: リストラ means being laid off (opposite of being wanted). アルバイト is part-time work, not a recruiting action.

contrast_examples.jp: ヘッドハンティングされた。

prompt.context_jp: 「私って どこまで ___ないんだろうなって…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私って どこまで ___ないんだろうなって…」
prompt.prompt_en: Miyuki complains about how unlucky she is.

feedback.correct_en: ツイてない means 'unlucky.' Miyuki is lamenting her lack of luck compared to easy-hire new grads.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持っていない means 'don't have (something).' 向いていない means 'not suited to.' Neither captures 'unlucky.'

contrast_examples.jp: この仕事は向いてない。

prompt.context_jp: 「あの坊やは どう見ても ___です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あの坊やは どう見ても ___です」
prompt.prompt_en: Haruko bluntly judges how the new recruit got hired.

feedback.correct_en: コネ入社 means getting hired through personal connections — matching Haruko's cutting assessment of Nasuda.
feedback.incorrect_en: 中途入社 means mid-career hire; 新卒入社 means new-graduate hire. Neither carries the critical 'via connections' meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 「"腹が___は 派遣はできぬ"」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「"腹が___は 派遣はできぬ"」
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the pun on 腹が減っては戦ができぬ (an army marches on its stomach).

feedback.correct_en: The famous proverb is 腹が減っては戦ができぬ (you can't fight on an empty stomach). The ad swaps 戦 for 派遣.
feedback.incorrect_en: 腹が立つ (to get angry) and 腹が痛い (stomachache) are real expressions but don't form this proverb.

contrast_examples.jp: 腹が減っては戦ができぬ。
contrast_examples.en: Can't fight on an empty stomach.

prompt.context_jp: Satonaka is withdrawing from the presentation before executives, speaking up to his boss Shoji.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Satonaka's reluctant refusal to present?

choices.text: 僕には プレゼンできません
僕は プレゼンするのが できない
私 プレゼン やらない

feedback.correct_en: The actual line uses 僕には...できません — natural polite refusal with the potential form marking inability for the speaker.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses awkward 'するのができない' which is ungrammatical; the potential form itself replaces でき+る. C is too casual and blunt for addressing a superior.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko's signature deadpan response when asked if she's received a call from Shoji.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line captures Haruko's characteristic cold brevity?

choices.text: ありませんが 何か？
いいえ、まだ連絡をいただいておりません

feedback.correct_en: ありませんが何か？ is Haruko's catchphrase — polite form plus a dismissive 'got a problem?' This brand of cool bluntness defines her.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly deferential business keigo — not Haruko's style. C is too friendly/casual with よ.

contrast_examples.en: No, there isn't. Got a problem?

contrast_examples.jp: 申し訳ございませんが、ありません。

prompt.context_jp: Haruko explains why she dislikes commute-time conversations with coworkers.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally captures 'I don't want you being over-familiar even during my commute'?

choices.text: 通勤時間まで なれなれしくされたくないからです
通勤時間まで 親切にされたくないからです
通勤時間まで 優しくされたくないからです

feedback.correct_en: なれなれしい carries the exact negative nuance of 'overly familiar / presumptuous' that Haruko needs. 親切 (kind) and 優しい (gentle) are positive, mismatching her complaint.
feedback.incorrect_en: B and C would make it sound like she objects to kindness itself, which misrepresents her actual boundary — she objects to coworker-intimacy bleeding into personal time.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko explains her philosophy of being a self-reliant temp.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Haruko's reflective monologue?

choices.text: 私は すがる人が いないから ここまで やってこれた
私は すがる人が いなかったから ここまで やってきたことができた
すがる人 私にいないから ここまで やってこれた

feedback.correct_en: A flows naturally with the potential form やってこれた (was able to come this far) tied cleanly to the reason clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is wordy and awkward ('やってきたことができた' is unidiomatic). C has disrupted word order with the particle misplaced.

contrast_examples.jp: 一人だから やってこれた。
contrast_examples.en: I could make it because I was alone.

contrast_examples.jp: 助けがあったから やってこれた。
contrast_examples.en: I could make it because I had help.

prompt.context_jp: Asano rebukes the gossiping employees during work hours.
prompt.prompt_en: Which scolding sounds most natural and in-character for strict Asano?

choices.text: そこの お時給泥棒 さっさと働きなさい！
そこの 時給泥棒さん すぐに働いていただけますか
時給の泥棒 働いて ください

feedback.correct_en: さっさと働きなさい has the sharp, scolding senpai tone Asano uses — the imperative なさい plus さっさと (quickly, snappily) fits her character.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's keigo request softens the scolding into absurdity. C is grammatically limp and lacks the biting rhythm.

contrast_examples.jp: 働いていただけますか。
